title: I found a hidden YouTube feature that is perfect for long videos
excerpt: This is one YouTube AI feature I'll keep
content_html:
Published Aug 9, 2026, 8:00 AM EDT

Sanuj is a freelance tech journalist with over six years of experience covering smartphones, wearables, and consumer technology. He currently writes for Android Police, Tom's Guide, Android Central, Android Authority, and Pocket-lint. He has previously contributed to publications like Pocketnow and MakeUseOf. 

Since the start of 2025 alone, he has tested over 30 smartphones. He has also attended major global trade shows including MWC (2024, 2025, 2026) and IFA (2024, 2025), along with launch events hosted by Google, Samsung, and other leading Android brands.

When he's not writing about tech, you'll find him sipping a cup of chai, scrolling Twitter, and reading updates about his favorite football club, Chelsea FC.

Feel free to reach out to him via email at sanujb6 [at] gmail [dot] com.

Want it or not, Google has slowly but surely filled almost every one of its products with AI.

Open any Google app or service, whether it's Google Docs, Google Maps, the Play Store, or Gmail, and chances are you'll find some form of Gemini integration built into it.

Some of those AI features have made life easier. Things like Gemini using local context to improve navigation in Google Maps or Help Me Write in Docs are actually useful.

Still, I've never been a fan of adding AI just for the sake of adding AI to products that don't really need it.

Or at least, that was my opinion at first.

When Google started bringing AI features to YouTube, I was firmly against the idea. But after using one particular feature for the past few weeks, I have to admit it completely changed my mind.

YouTube AI is surprisingly useful for finding video timestamps

It helps me jump to the right moment without scrubbing through long videos

When Google introduced the Ask Videos feature in YouTube, my immediate reaction was, "Why would anyone use this when they're *literally* watching the video they want to ask questions about?"

It didn't make much sense to me. If I'm watching a video, I'd rather hear the creator explain something than ask an AI model to summarize it for me. Besides, AI can make mistakes, and Google warns users about that.

But over the past few weeks, I've found one use case that has completely changed my opinion of this feature, and that is generating rough timestamps for videos.

Google already lets creators add chapters to their videos and generates them automatically during upload. The problem is that not every YouTube video has chapters.

If you're watching a 40-minute or 1-hour video, finding a specific section usually means scrubbing through the timeline until you stumble upon it.

Ask Videos solves that surprisingly well. Instead of manually searching, I ask Gemini to generate rough timestamps for the video.

Within a few seconds, it gives me a breakdown of the main topics along with approximate timestamps, and I can tap any of them to jump to that section.

Using the Ask Videos feature on YouTube is simple:

  1. Open the YouTube video you want to watch.
  2. Tap the Gemini icon in the action bar next to the Like, Dislike, and Share buttons.
  3. Type your question or prompt into the text box.

When you open the Gemini pop-up on the video page, YouTube suggests a few prompts depending on the video you're watching. For example, if it's an EV review, you'll see shortcuts to ask about performance, range, practicality, and other topics.

However, I mostly use this feature to generate timestamps for videos that don't already have them.

I type something like "Generate rough timestamps for this video," and Gemini returns a fairly detailed outline of the video's sections along with approximate timestamps, so I can jump to the part I'm interested in by tapping the timestamp.

This is a feature I think students will especially appreciate, particularly when watching long educational videos that cover multiple topics.

Even if you're in a hurry and only want to watch one specific section, it's a faster way to get there than scrubbing through the timeline.

But I also want AI to help remove AI-generated videos from my feed

YouTube needs a simple toggle to hide AI slop from recommendations

While I've come around to some of YouTube's AI features, there's another AI-related issue that bothers me far more: the flood of AI-generated videos in my recommendations.

Thanks to tools like Google's Omni and other video-generative AI platforms, creating videos has become incredibly easy.

Unfortunately, that also means my YouTube home feed is increasingly filled with AI-generated content that I have absolutely no interest in watching.

It feels like my recommendations have become cluttered with AI slop, and I wish there were a toggle to hide those videos altogether.

I'd love YouTube to introduce an option that lets users opt out of AI-generated content in their recommendations. In my opinion, that would do more to improve YouTube than many of the AI features the company announced recently.

Judging by how many people are complaining online, I know I'm not the only one who's tired of seeing AI slop take over their feeds.

The next step should be giving us control over AI-generated content

AI itself isn't the problem. It's how people choose to use it. We've heard this before, and YouTube is probably the best example.

The Ask videos feature is genuinely useful, and it's one AI feature I've started relying on. But at the same time, AI-generated videos that exist purely to farm views make the platform noticeably worse.

So yes, I think Google has done a good job integrating AI into YouTube. I've also found Gemini useful for things like staying on top of bills and planning trips.

But if YouTube is going to keep embracing AI, I think it also owes users better control over how much AI-generated content they want to see.

content_html_zh:
发布于 2026 年 8 月 9 日，美国东部时间上午 8:00

Sanuj 是一名自由科技记者，在智能手机、可穿戴设备和消费技术领域拥有超过六年的经验。 他目前为 Android Police、Tom's Guide、Android Central、Android Authority 和 Pocket-lint 撰写文章。 他之前曾为 Pocketnow 和 MakeUseOf 等出版物做出过贡献。

仅自 2025 年初以来，他就测试了 30 多款智能手机。 他还参加了 MWC（2024 年、2025 年、2026 年）和 IFA（2024 年、2025 年）等主要全球贸易展，以及由 Google、三星和其他领先 Android 品牌主办的发布会。

当他不写科技文章时，你会发现他喝着一杯奶茶，浏览推特，阅读有关他最喜欢的足球俱乐部切尔西足球俱乐部的更新。

请随时通过电子邮件与他联系：sanujb6 [at] gmail [dot] com。

不管你愿意不愿意，谷歌已经缓慢但坚定地在其几乎每一款产品中都融入了人工智能。

打开任何 Google 应用程序或服务，无论是 Google 文档、Google 地图、Play 商店还是 Gmail，您很可能会发现其中内置了某种形式的 Gemini 集成。

其中一些人工智能功能让生活变得更轻松。 像 Gemini 使用本地上下文来改进 Google 地图中的导航或帮助我在文档中编写之类的东西实际上很有用。

尽管如此，我从来不热衷于仅仅为了将人工智能添加到并不真正需要它的产品中而添加人工智能。

或者至少，一开始我是这么认为的。

当谷歌开始将人工智能功能引入 YouTube 时，我坚决反对这个想法。 但在过去几周使用了一项特定功能后，我不得不承认它完全改变了我的想法。

YouTube AI 对于查找视频时间戳非常有用

它可以帮助我跳到正确的时刻，而无需浏览长视频

当谷歌在 YouTube 中推出“提问视频”功能时，我的第一反应是，“当人们‘真正’观看他们想要提问的视频时，为什么会使用这个功能呢？”

这对我来说没有多大意义。 如果我正在观看视频，我宁愿听创作者解释一些内容，也不愿让人工智能模型为我进行总结。 此外，人工智能可能会犯错误，谷歌警告用户这一点。

但在过去的几周里，我发现一个用例完全改变了我对此功能的看法，那就是为视频生成粗略的时间戳。

谷歌已经允许创作者在他们的视频中添加章节并在上传过程中自动生成。 问题是并非每个 YouTube 视频都有章节。

如果您正在观看 40 分钟或 1 小时的视频，要找到特定部分通常意味着要在时间轴中滑动，直到偶然发现它。

Ask Videos 出人意料地很好地解决了这个问题。 我没有手动搜索，而是要求 Gemini 为视频生成粗略的时间戳。

几秒钟之内，它就为我提供了主要主题的细分以及大概的时间戳，我可以点击其中任何一个来跳转到该部分。

使用 YouTube 上的“询问视频”功能非常简单：

  1. 打开您要观看的 YouTube 视频。
  2. 点击操作栏中“喜欢”、“不喜欢”和“分享”按钮旁边的双子座图标。
  3. 在文本框中输入您的问题或提示。

当您打开视频页面上的 Gemini 弹出窗口时，YouTube 会根据您正在观看的视频提出一些提示。 例如，如果是电动汽车评论，您会看到询问性能、续航里程、实用性和其他主题的快捷方式。

但是，我主要使用此功能为尚无时间戳的视频生成时间戳。

我输入类似“为此视频生成粗略时间戳”之类的内容，Gemini 返回视频各部分的相当详细的轮廓以及大致时间戳，因此我可以通过点击时间戳跳转到我感兴趣的部分。

我认为学生会特别喜欢这个功能，特别是在观看涵盖多个主题的长教育视频时。

即使您很赶时间并且只想观看某个特定部分，这也是比浏览时间线更快的方式。

但我也希望人工智能能够帮助从我的动态中删除人工智能生成的视频

YouTube 需要一个简单的开关来隐藏推荐中的 AI 错误

虽然我已经开始接受 YouTube 的一些人工智能功能，但还有另一个与人工智能相关的问题更让我困扰：我的推荐中充斥着人工智能生成的视频。

借助 Google Omni 和其他视频生成人工智能平台等工具，创建视频变得异常简单。

不幸的是，这也意味着我的 YouTube 主播中越来越多地充满了我完全没有兴趣观看的人工智能生成的内容。

感觉我的推荐已经被人工智能的废话弄乱了，我希望有一个开关可以完全隐藏这些视频。

我希望 YouTube 能够推出一个选项，让用户可以在推荐中选择退出人工智能生成的内容。 在我看来，这比该公司最近宣布的许多人工智能功能更能改善 YouTube。

从有多少人在网上抱怨来看，我知道我并不是唯一一个厌倦了看到人工智能接管他们的信息流的人。

下一步应该是让我们控制人工智能生成的内容

人工智能本身并不是问题。 这就是人们选择使用它的方式。 我们以前听说过这个，YouTube 可能是最好的例子。

“询问视频”功能确实很有用，它是我开始依赖的一项人工智能功能。 但与此同时，纯粹为了吸引观看次数而存在的人工智能生成视频使该平台明显变得更糟。

所以，是的，我认为谷歌在将人工智能融入 YouTube 方面做得很好。 我还发现双子座对于掌握账单和计划旅行等事情很有用。

但如果 YouTube 要继续拥抱人工智能，我认为用户还应该更好地控制他们想要看到多少人工智能生成的内容。
